# Data Preparation and Feature Engineering

## Learning Objectives
- Diagnose data-quality problems.
- Handle missing, categorical, and scaled features appropriately.
- Explain data leakage and prevent it with pipelines.
- Engineer features using substantive knowledge.
- Build preprocessing workflows with scikit-learn.

## Why This Matters
Model quality is constrained by data quality, and seemingly harmless preprocessing can invalidate an evaluation if information leaks across data partitions.

## Real-World Problem
A preprocessing workflow standardizes the entire dataset before the train-test split. Why is the resulting performance estimate potentially optimistic?

## Hands-On Practice
Construct a preprocessing pipeline for mixed numeric and categorical data.

## Common Mistakes
- Preprocessing before splitting.
- Imputing using information from the test set.
- Encoding identifiers as meaningful numeric features.
- Feature engineering using future information.

## Knowledge Check
1. Why can scaling cause leakage?
2. When is one-hot encoding appropriate?
3. What does a Pipeline protect against?
4. Why should identifiers usually be excluded?

## Real-World Case Study
### Preparing Public Education Data for Modeling
Develop a documented feature matrix from an institutional dataset.

## Professor's Challenge
Two analysts obtain different model results from the same raw data. How would you audit their preprocessing pipelines?

## Research Extension
Compare alternative missing-data or feature-engineering strategies using nested evaluation.

## Reproducibility Check
Preserve raw data, script transformations, document exclusions, and keep preprocessing inside the modeling workflow.

## Key Takeaways
- Preprocessing is part of the model.
- Leakage can invalidate otherwise sophisticated analyses.
- Feature engineering should combine technical and domain knowledge.
